Tessa / Ben —

Attached is Wilson LLP's proposed redline to the DPA & the SCCs mapping for EverHealth's order form. Key items flagged on page 3 (export paths) and clause 6.2 (processor roles) that will need operational confirmation:

- Export paths: EverHealth's procurement team is asking for a carveout where analytics outputs destined for the EU require an additional EEA-only subprocessor list.
- Roles: The redline converts some controller/processor language to a hybrid approach for derivative outputs — we need clarity on whether Redwood will be a processor for telemetry and analytics outputs or a controller for aggregated metrics.
- KMS / key custody: Proposed language requires demonstration of KMS separation for customer-managed keys (page 7).

ActionRequested: Please confirm Redwood's operational stance and provide any evidence we can share (subprocessor list, KMS diagram, export routing controls).

Attachments: DPA_redline_EverHealth_v2.docx, SCCs_export_map.csv

Subject: Re: EverHealth - initial DPA redline and SCCs alignment

Thanks Rachel — good summary. Looping in Ben and Karthik for ops + infra confirmation. Quick answers up front:

- Export routing: Redwood can enforce EEA-only routing for processing of raw customer PII when requested via the order form; analytics-derived aggregates are by default stored in our multi-region analytics tier unless explicitly scoped to EEA-only.
- Roles: We treat telemetry/usage metrics as "service improvement" processor activity. Aggregated business metrics that include customer identifiers are handled per customer configuration — there is a setting in the onboarding order form to make Redwood a processor-only for those outputs.
- KMS: We support both Redwood-managed and customer-managed keys via KMS integration (we use customer keys for encryption-at-rest when requested). Will confirm diagram and HSM details.

I'll capture concrete evidence and a short description for legal by EOD. Two asks for the EverHealth team:
1) Can EverHealth confirm whether they will require analytics outputs classified as PII to be treated with export restrictions (i.e., not leave EEA)?
2) If EverHealth wants EEA-only analytics, we'll need the order form flag set and an SLA amendment for retention zones — can you flag that with procurement/contact?

-Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Head of Customer Compliance, Redwood Inference

Oliver — appreciate the clarity. Summary of the operational deliverables we will provide by EOD PST tomorrow:

1) KMS / key custody document (1 page diagram + bullet list) — explains how customer-managed keys are integrated, HSM vendor, and separation controls.
2) Subprocessor roster (CSV) with region columns and data processing purpose.
3) Draft language for clause 6.2 that preserves Redwood as processor for telemetry/improvement signals but treats analytics outputs containing customer personal data as subject to the customer's export-routing selection (EEA-only when flagged).

Proposed 6.2 snippet (for redline):
"When Customer elects the EEA-only analytics option in the Order Form, Processor shall ensure that any analytics outputs that contain or are derived from Customer Personal Data originating in the EEA are processed and stored exclusively within EEA-hosted infrastructure, and shall not export such outputs outside the EEA except as strictly required by law and with prior written notice to Customer."

We will include an appendix mapping SCC clauses affected by this behavior.
